summary: Bollinger BandWidth: the gap between the bands as a share of the middle line, with squeeze and bulge levels over 125 bars.
overview: Bollinger BandWidth shows how wide the Bollinger Bands are, in its own pane. Low values mean tight bands and quiet price; high values mean wide bands.
It also draws a squeeze level (the lowest width of the last 125 bars) and a bulge level (the highest).
how: BandWidth = (upper band - lower band) / basis. The bands use a 20-bar SMA and 2 standard deviations by default.
When the line reaches the squeeze level it takes the squeeze color; at the bulge level it takes the bulge color.
use: Some traders watch for a squeeze as a sign a quiet period may end with a larger move.
Use the bulge level to see volatility that is unusually high for the window.
Use it with price to choose a direction, since width shows none.
Compare widths over time to see the symbol's normal range.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
A squeeze is a condition, not a direction.
